text:
Leah Kim: Heads-up — Heliotrope POC asking for a one-page network summary: VPC peering vs PrivateLink, exact SG/firewall lines they can paste into their questionnaire, and whether Redwood ever needs inbound rules. POC starts 2024-09-02. cc @Diego Ramos @Maya Singh

Diego Ramos: TL;DR: both options supported. Use VPC peering for best throughput/latency if CIDRs don’t overlap. Use AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints) when CIDRs overlap or customer policy forbids peering.

Maya Singh: Paste-ready SG snippet (AWS):
- CUSTOMER_SG outbound: TCP 443 -> 52.198.10.0/24 (Redwood control plane egress list)
- If PrivateLink: CUSTOMER_SG outbound: TCP 443 -> <ENI_IP_RANGES_CREATED_BY_AWS>
- If VPC peering: CUSTOMER_SG outbound: TCP 443, TCP 50051 -> <REWOOD_PEER_CIDR_EXAMPLE 10.201.0.0/16>
- For streaming: ensure stable NAT EIP(s) or use an egress proxy.

Oliver Hart: Security clarifications: we terminate TLS at our control plane. For Private deployments we can enable mTLS on control plane RPC port 50051 on request. We publish a live JSON of IP ranges customers can allowlist — recommend referring to that rather than hardcoding.

Leah Kim: Do we ever require inbound rules on the customer VPC?

Diego Ramos: No for normal customer-initiated traffic — everything is outbound from customer to Redwood. Exception: custom integrations where Redwood needs to reach into customer's VPC (rare) — those are handled via a change request and documented inbound rules.

Maya Singh: Overlap workaround: PrivateLink preferred. Alternate: customer creates a transit/non-overlapping VPC and NAT/proxy to us. Avoid CIDR renumbering if possible.

redwood-bot: Draft uploaded: docs/presales/1720501234-heliotrope-net-onepager.pdf -> s3://redwood-internal/docs-presales/1720501234-heliotrope-net-onepager.pdf

Leah Kim: Great — I'll attach this to the security questionnaire and send to Heliotrope sec team. Anyone want to add contact emails for escalation?

Oliver Hart: Add infra-ops@redwood.ai and se-oncall@redwood.ai. No blockers from security.

Diego Ramos: I'll add a tiny diagram and a two-line FAQ before EOD.

Leah Kim: Thanks all :thumbsup:
